author: Old Dominion News
title: Old Dominion adds transfer guard Bubu Benjamin to men's basketball roster
text:
Old Dominion University men’s basketball head coach Mike Jones announced on June 10 the addition of transfer guard Bubu Benjamin to the Monarchs’ 2026-27 roster. Benjamin, a 6-foot 7-inch guard from George Washington, is one of seven transfers joining the team for the upcoming season.
Jones said, “One of our goals this offseason was to get more positional size without sacrificing the offensive end of the floor. Bubu does that for us as a guard with great size and a skill set that has been proven on this level. He will impact on both ends of the floor – his versatility, toughness, IQ and playmaking will be a huge asset for us. He is a natural leader and Monarch Nation will love the passion that Bubu plays with.”
A native of Medicine Hat, Alberta, Canada, Benjamin began his collegiate career at Tarleton State. In his freshman year during the 2023-24 season, he appeared in 22 games with an average of 2.8 points and 1.7 rebounds per game. His sophomore season saw significant improvement as he led Tarleton State in several categories including points per game (13.9), total points (446), made free throws (97), made three-pointers (49), and minutes per game (36). He finished first in minutes per game in the Western Athletic Conference and ranked fourth in steals (48), seventh in free-throw shooting percentage (78.9%), and eighth in points per game.
Benjamin transferred to George Washington for his junior year, where he started 18 out of 30 games played and averaged 5.8 points along with 2.7 rebounds per contest over an average of just over twenty minutes each outing.
Over three collegiate seasons, Benjamin has accumulated career totals including 681 points at an average rate exceeding eight points per contest while shooting over forty-two percent from the field.
Before college, Benjamin played four years at Edge School where he set a school record by scoring forty-three points in one game and represented Canada internationally at both U18 and U19 levels—including earning bronze at the FIBA U18 Americas Championship.
